title: A world worth watching
changes: A compact civilization ribbon shows actual people, towns and current work. Readable town sheets and a short Chronicle keep the map in view, with detailed records still available.

Warmer terrain, layered shores, varied trees and clearer inhabited rooftops reveal the same world. Optional event following moves only the camera; manual exploration pauses it, and reduced motion is respected.

title: Connection can grow over land
changes: After states rise, an ordinary-founded town can earn Connected world through a real paid exchange with a foreign town over land. Its founding and exact exchange remain recorded; coastal development is still another path.
Industry and Mars still need their separate physical achievements. This opens an earned historical alternative, not a promised expansion or automatic advance of the calendar.

title: Make room for a possible coastal town
changes: A civilization can compare retaining one productive operation with freeing its three residents for a fully supplied coastal opportunity. Food, Learning and accepted commitments remain protected.
Pausing is optional preparation, not a promised departure. A later settlement is independently chosen and pays its actual founding costs; hypothetical town output is never spent in advance.
